criteria.new_defect: The new review reports a defect the previous review did not, other than the priorities this move targeted.
criteria.no_new_defect: The new review reports nothing the previous one did not, beyond what this move was aiming at.

side_effects.instructions: Does the new review report a defect that the previous review did not, other than the priorities this move targeted? This question is uncalibrated: no labelled set stands behind it.

state.meaning: A move that fixed what it aimed at and broke something else is not an improvement.

defects: Both renders have a narrow ovoid-to-columnar crown that is clearly taller than it is wide: about 490 px wide by 840 px tall in render-0, and about 440 px by 800 px in render-1. The reference crown is broad, domed to flat-topped, and about as wide as it is tall or wider.

In neither render do the limbs fan out and arch to near-horizontal or drooping at the crown edge. The visible limbs are mostly straight and steeply ascending. Bare limb tips stick out past the foliage at the crown top.
The crown surface in both renders is an even, fuzzy leaf texture. It lacks the flat-to-drooping, layered, lacy sprays with distinct tips against the sky that the reference shows.
In render-1 the bole splits into several spreading limbs at about 24% of the tree's height, with a central stem carrying on upward. This is not a narrow two-leader V at about 40-45%.
In render-1 the clear bole ends at about 24% of the tree's height. The reference is clear to about 40%.
Both render crowns are dense, with little sky or internal structure showing through. The reference crown is open and made of many small clusters.
observations: Render-0 and render-1 both show a pale, silvery-grey, even-toned trunk with no furrows. This matches reference-0.

Render-0 has one straight bole. The trunk shows through the foliage up to about 40% of the tree's height, but drooping foliage hides where the branches start below that, so the clear-bole height can't be confirmed.
In render-1 the limbs visibly leave the bole at about 24% of the tree's height. The reference bole is clear to about 40%.
In render-0 two pale stems seem to run side by side inside the lower crown, but foliage hides the fork, so a codominant V can't be confirmed.
In render-1 there is a low, several-way split at about 24% of the tree's height, and a central leader carries on upward. The reference has a narrow two-leader V at about 42%.
In both renders the crown is a narrow upright oval, about 0.55 times as wide as it is tall. The reference crown is broad, domed to flat-topped, and at least as wide as it is tall.
The limbs in both renders stay steep and straight, and bare tips stick out at the top. They do not fan out or arch to horizontal or drooping at the edge as in the reference.
The crown edge in both renders is an even, fuzzy particle texture. It lacks the reference's distinct flat, drooping, layered spray tips.
Both render crowns are mostly solid, with only small sky gaps. The reference is open and shows its internal branch structure.
Leaf shape can't be resolved in the renders or in the reference, so there is nothing to compare.
Both renders show a slight flare at the trunk base. The darker tone seen in the reference is not reproduced, but the inventory leaves its cause undetermined.

Both renders are at or above the finish floor set by the Norway spruce anchor (anchor-0). This is a finish comparison only and says nothing about morphology.
The trunks in both renders match the reference's pale grey, even-toned, straight single bole.
The main defining mismatch is overall habit: both renders read as a narrow, upright oval tree (poplar- or hornbeam-like), not the reference's broad, umbrella-like open-grown beech.
The crown runs down to about 24% of the tree's height in both renders. In the reference it starts at about 40-45%.
Leaf colour (fresh-yellow-green-leaf-colour), crown-asymmetry, lower-drooping-foliage-right and open-grown-habit are variation traits in the inventory and were not treated as blockers.

defects: Both seeds render a narrow columnar crown with a pointed top, like a Lombardy poplar. The crown is about 2.5-3x taller than it is wide. The reference shows a broad, domed to flat-topped crown that is about as wide as it is tall.
Foliage starts about 10-15% up the tree in both seeds. The reference has a clear, branch-free bole for about 40% of its height.
The trunk splits low, at about 10-15% of the height, into three or more steep, near-parallel stems. The reference splits into two co-dominant leaders in a narrow V at about 40-45% of the height.
The limbs stay steeply upright up to the crown edge. They never fan outward or arch to near-horizontal and droop, as the reference limbs do.
The crown edge is a uniform fuzzy fringe of upright foliage. It lacks the reference's flat-to-drooping, layered sprays with individual spray tips standing out against the sky.
The foliage is a dense, mostly solid mass. Little sky or internal branch structure shows through, whereas the reference crown is open and translucent.
observations: Crown silhouette: both renders show a tall, narrow column with a pointed top (width about 0.35-0.4 of height). The reference crown is broad and domed, about as wide as it is tall or wider.
The clear bole ends at about 10-15% of the tree's height in both renders, versus about 40% in the reference.
Both renders split low into several steep, parallel stems. Neither shows a two-leader narrow V at 40-45% of the height.
The visible pale limbs in the renders stay steeply ascending all the way to the crown edge, with no outward arching or droop. The reference's dark limbs fan out and droop near the edge.
The render crown edge is fine-grained but upright and uniform. It does not show the reference's layered, drooping sprays.
The render crowns are dense and mostly opaque. The reference crown is open, with sky and branches visible throughout.
Both render trunks are pale silvery grey and even-toned, with only faint horizontal marks and no furrows. This is consistent with the reference trunk.
Both render trunks visibly flare at the base. The darker base seen in the reference is absent, but its cause is undetermined, so this counts as acceptable variation.
Leaf shape cannot be resolved in the reference or at the renders' viewing distance, so there is no basis for comparison.
The render foliage is mid-to-bright green rather than the reference's pale yellow-green. The inventory classes leaf colour as seasonal variation.
The render crowns are nearly symmetric, while the reference is right-heavy. The inventory classes this asymmetry as variation.

render-0 (seed 1) and render-1 (seed 42) both show one tree with a narrow, spindle-shaped columnar crown and a pointed apex. The reference-0 tree has a broad, flat-domed, mushroom-like crown on a tall clear bole.
Render finish (bark shading, leaf density, lighting) meets or exceeds anchor-0's stylistic floor, so finish quality is not the limiting factor. The failures are in species morphology.
The pale grey, smooth-looking trunk with a flared base is the only strong beech cue the renders reproduce.
Neither seed would be read as an open-grown European beech. Their silhouette suggests a fastigiate poplar or hornbeam cultivar instead.

targeted.improved: Across the set, the crown widens from columnar through ovoid to a broad dome and then a flat top. The foliage opens up and the limbs start to spread and arch.
looks_wrong: Ovoid crown, taller than it is wide, where the reference is broad and domed
Dense, uniform foliage mass with little sky or limb structure showing through
targeted.missing: None of the renders has the clear two-leader V fork at mid-height with dark scaffold limbs fanning through a light, open crown. Bare spike-like branch tips also remain in the broader renders.
